conditions: The same designed actor reacts to a visible outdoor light in the tested head and torso range
counterexamples: This does not approve hand or curtain contact
A natural join in this shot does not establish full-body or cross-script acting
cases.failure: C retained the liked light and face response but its neck and clothing assembly was visibly discontinuous.
cases.correction: D preserved the existing light and face timing while reauthoring the neck-to-collar join.
cases.result: The user judged D much more natural than C and explicitly confirmed the neck and clothing join looks natural. Comprehension and full acting remain unmeasured.
cases.next_experiment: Bind the D actor's exact artwork and permitted pose range, then inspect the full motion path and independently authored arm/curtain contact before testing another script.

conditions: A visible outdoor lamp illuminates a resting character before the character reacts
counterexamples: Not a requirement for intentionally hidden causes
This approval does not establish comprehension gain or rig correctness
cases.failure: Earlier version communicated tiredness but little noticing.
cases.correction: Visible lamp onset, illumination reaching the face, then eye response, squint and head response.
cases.result: User explicitly likes lighting, facial expression and response in C, initially called B by the user. Neck/clothing continuity remains REVISE.
cases.next_experiment: Repair the neck while preserving approved lighting, expression and response timing; compare against this exact video before changing the performance.

conditions: Separately authored head and torso meet on a visible shaded skin surface
counterexamples: Flat artwork may intentionally have distinct color fields
Color difference by itself can be legitimate lighting
cases.failure: Opaque skin patch covered the neckline hole but introduced an angular shading boundary. The head and patch had independent motion and lighting.
cases.correction: Do not call coverage a finished join. Require common-source registration, authored overlap, motion binding and localized full-frame evidence before human review.
cases.result: C assembly remains REVISE. Later user clarification approves C lighting, expression and response only; preserve those while repairing the joint. No repaired successor is approved.
cases.next_experiment: Author a continuous neck in one layered document, reconstruct rest pose, then sweep the permitted head motion. Compare against C with unchanged narration.

conditions: An environmental stimulus should visibly interrupt a resting character
counterexamples: Deliberately concealed off-screen causes may be appropriate in suspense
Tiredness alone does not demonstrate perception or comprehension
cases.failure: Human review: noticing was weak, emotion read as tiredness, neckline was transparent, and comprehension was no better than baseline.
cases.correction: Experimental C adds a visible source and face-reaching illumination, eye-before-head timing, opaque neck coverage, and a fixed cheek support pivot. C lighting and acting later received scoped human approval; neck coverage still fails assembly review.
cases.result: B v2 requires revision. C lighting, expression and response are liked by the user; information-comprehension improvement and cross-script transfer remain unmeasured.
cases.next_experiment: Compare B and C using identical narration. Ask what caused the reaction before showing the intended answer. Evaluate comprehension separately from emotion and assembly defects.

conditions: The scene communicates transport and elapsed movement matters
counterexamples: A conceptual loop may deliberately abstract source timing
One region's flow cannot represent every object's motion
cases.failure: Replacing a time series by median speed reduced measured total displacement from 179.72 to approximately 139.94 pixels.
cases.correction: Preserve cumulative displacement and source timestamps; reject missing intervals rather than treating them as stationary.
cases.next_experiment: Transfer cumulative transport to independently designed GPU task tokens; compare completion order and arrival timing with equal narration. Human review must assess causal clarity.

conditions: Separate moving units must remain individually legible
counterexamples: Intentional aggregation or occlusion may be meaningful
A no-overlap score does not prove appealing design or natural motion
cases.failure: Modulo placement created near-duplicate positions; fixed-radius checks could become stale after a design change.
cases.correction: Use explicit spacing and validate actual rendered geometry; retain visual review independently from collision checks.
cases.next_experiment: Use different-shaped computation tokens in a new GPU scene; test silhouette changes and label readability without reusing ellipse-only assumptions.

conditions: Two visual domains share one frame and objects must remain within their assigned domain
counterexamples: An object may deliberately cross the boundary to demonstrate a transition
Clipping alone does not establish that the comparison is understood
cases.failure: V1 city silhouette extended across the dark-sky half of an 80% skyglow comparison.
cases.correction: Bind the city object to an explicit left-half clip region and verify both halves in rendered frames.
cases.result: V2 frame shows the city only on the light-polluted half; viewer comprehension has not been tested.
cases.next_experiment: Use a new topic with a different split-layout asset to test whether clip-region contracts prevent cross-panel bleed without hiding intended transitions.

conditions: An SVG actor has a designed scene-space anchor and an independent local motion path
counterexamples: A scene may intentionally animate its root anchor
In-frame bounds do not prove an anatomically credible pose or correct destination
cases.failure: V1 bird and turtle were partly off-screen because GSAP movement replaced their authored SVG transform.
cases.correction: Keep the scene-space anchor on a parent group and animate a child group in local coordinates; review sampled path frames.
cases.result: V2 sampled frame shows both objects inside the scene; the entire path and emotional reading await separate review.
cases.next_experiment: Animate a different anchored actor along a new route, measure the full path and compare scene-space coordinates with the rendered silhouette.
